metadata.name: Ecodesign for Rust
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Rust code: allocations under control, iterators without materialisation, non-blocking async, sober dependencies.

allocations.name: Rust — allocations and copies
allocations.description: Rust is sober by design; the point is not to squander that advantage (RGESN Algorithms, GR491_Backend_4).

rules.title: Convenience clone()
rules.description: Cloning to work around the borrow checker allocates and copies data you could have borrowed.
rules.recommendation: Borrow (&) when ownership is not required; Cow<str> for the sometimes-owned cases; expose &str and &[T] in signatures.

rules.title: Intermediate collect() in an iterator chain
rules.description: Every collect materialises a temporary Vec: an allocation and a copy for a value consumed immediately afterwards.
rules.recommendation: Chain the iterators without an intermediate collect; materialise only the final result, with with_capacity when the size is known.

rules.title: Vec with no pre-reserved capacity
rules.description: A Vec growing through successive reallocations copies its content at every doubling.
rules.recommendation: Vec::with_capacity(n) when the size is predictable; reuse buffers in hot loops (clear() keeps the capacity).

async.name: Rust — async and I/O
async.description: Do not block the executor, reuse clients, bound the queues (RGESN Backend).

rules.title: Blocking call inside an async task
rules.description: A sleep or a long computation inside an async task blocks an executor worker and freezes the other tasks.
rules.recommendation: spawn_blocking or a dedicated thread for long CPU work; tokio::time::sleep on the async side; buffered I/O (BufReader/BufWriter) and streaming for large volumes.

rules.title: Network client created per request
rules.description: reqwest::Client::new() per call repeats the TLS handshake and loses the connection pool.
rules.recommendation: Create the client once and clone it (the pool is shared); bounded channels and caches to avoid uncontrolled memory growth.

build.name: Rust — dependencies and build
build.description: Lighten the dependency graph and avoid needless restarts (RGESN Architecture/Hosting).

rules.title: unwrap() on an expected error path
rules.description: A panic on a foreseeable error restarts the service: recovery, a cold cache, and computation redone at every incident.
rules.recommendation: Handle the error (Result, ?) on expected paths; keep unwrap for invariants that are genuinely guaranteed.

rules.title: Unjustified dependency graph
rules.description: Every crate, and every feature enabled by default, weighs on compilation, on the binary and on the maintenance surface.
rules.recommendation: Justify each crate, disable unused features (default-features = false), check with cargo tree; build production with --release.
